You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

New instance. Task id: task-30861639
Test input (1x12):
5 0 1 3 4 3 7 6 9 3 2 8
Wrong attempts used: 0/8. Demo requests used: 0/8.
Reply with exactly one action JSON on the last line.

steps.output: [('arc_mirrored_tripling_of_grid_dimensions', 'ARC mirrored tripling of grid dimensions', 'Continual-ARC pattern: given an HxW input grid, output has size 3H x 2W. Each output row is formed by concatenating the row reversed left-to-right, then the original row. The output row sequence is reversed(input rows) + input rows + reversed(input rows). Demonstrations: 5x4 became 15x8; 1x7 became 3x14. For the 1-row case, reversing the one-row sequence gives three identical output rows. Be precise: vertical order is [rows reversed, rows forward, rows reversed], not simply triplicate each input row; source rows at each of the three positions in each output block follow this sequence.'), ('arc_grid_clue_intersections_determine_output_cells', 'ARC grid clue intersections determine output cells', 'For Continual-ARC tasks with a large regular tiled grid, thin separator lines (often color X) cross at vertices. The interiors of tiles have a uniform base color B. Special colors are written at some separator intersections; unmarked intersections retain separator color X. Crop to the rectangular vertex region spanning all clue-bearing intersections (those differing from separator color), including every regular separator vertex between min/max marked row/column. For each adjacent-vertex rectangle, output one cell: if its four corner intersection values are all identical, use that common color; otherwise use the tile-interior base color B. Output dimensions are (number of selected horizontal vertex lines - 1) × (number of selected vertical vertex lines - 1). Example solved task-53f0c104: X=0, B=9; marked vertex rows r14,r19,r24 and cols c5,c8,c11,c14,c17,c20,c23; output [[6,9,9,9,9,7],[6,6,9,3,9,7]].
